Combine nearby stops

Source: R/combine_nearby_stops.R
combine_nearby_stops.Rd

Merges the stops that are within a given distance of each other into a single stop, and updates the tables that refer to them. Useful to build routing networks or to analyse the feed by station rather than by platform.

Usage

combine_nearby_stops(gtfs, max_dist)

Arguments

gtfs

A GTFS object, as created by read_gtfs().

max_dist

A number. The maximum distance, in meters, between two stops merged together.

Value

The GTFS object with the merged stops.

Details

Stops with a parent_station are always merged into one stop with the stop_id of the parent station, regardless of the distance between them. This stop is named after the parent station if it's listed in stops, or else after its platforms. Then stops are merged by distance, so that every pair of stops merged together is at most max_dist apart. The closest pairs are merged first. Stops that were already merged by their parent station are compared by the mean of their coordinates, so their own platforms may be farther apart. Distances are great-circle distances, as in get_stop_distances(). Stops without coordinates are only merged by their parent station.

A stop merged from several stops has a stop_id and a stop_name made of the ids and names of the merged stops, separated by "-" (repeated names are listed only once), and the mean of their coordinates. Its other fields, such as zone_id and level_id, are those of the merged stop whose stop_id comes first. If a stop_id is listed more than once in stops, only its first entry is used.

The result has only plain stops (location_type 0) without parent_station: stations are replaced by the stop merged from their platforms, and stations without platforms, entrances, generic nodes, boarding areas and pathways are removed. The stop_ids of merged stops and stations are updated in stop_times, transfers, stop_areas, location_group_stops and fare_leg_join_rules, but references to removed stops are left as they are. Transfers between stops that were merged together become transfers within the merged stop, and when several transfers end up with the same stops, routes and trips, only the first one is kept, even if their transfer_type or min_transfer_time differ. The other fields of transfers are not changed, so a min_transfer_time between platforms that were merged now applies within the merged stop, and may no longer be accurate. Since transfers is optional, it can be removed (gtfs$transfers <- NULL) when these rules are not needed. Duplicated rows of stop_areas and location_group_stops are removed. Translations of merged stops are not updated. References to removed stops and their translations can be removed with remove_unused_ids().

An error is raised if max_dist is so large that all stops would be merged into a single one. Large values of max_dist in dense feeds compare many pairs of stops, which is slow and raises a warning when it may use a lot of memory, or an error when there are too many pairs to compare.

Merged stop_ids can be long at large terminals, and are ambiguous when the original stop_ids include "-". Feeds that cross the antimeridian are not supported.

See also

get_stop_distances(), merge_gtfs()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo_gtfs.zip", package = "gtfstools")
gtfs <- read_gtfs(data_path)
nrow(gtfs$stops)
#> [1] 654

combined_gtfs <- combine_nearby_stops(gtfs, max_dist = 100)
nrow(combined_gtfs$stops)
#> [1] 487
